a) the converter can be operated with a reduced number of switches, b) the battery storage elements can be balanced in a simple and effective manner, c) the grid faults can be handled in an appropriate manner and d) the converter operation is not affected by grid asymmetries.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the control and balancing of the active components of a Cascaded H-Bidge converter with embedded battery storage, in the context of a three-phase AC grid.
the development of a control strategy that is able to handle all these modes, in order to ensure the safe operation of the system.
the control of the converter and the storage elements in order to achieve the desired performance, while taking into account the converter topology and the specific constraints imposed by the system.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the proposed methods are able to achieve the control objectives with the least number of control loops and with the lowest possible number of active switches, while the converter is operated under the most severe grid asymmetries.
the proposed control strategies allow for a flexible utilization of the converter modules, which can be used for both active power and balancing purposes.

, for the delta configuration, the converter can operate with only two active components, which are the two active modules, while, for the star configuration, only three active components are required, which are the three active modules.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed control algorithms allow the cascaded H-bridges to operate with a high degree of independence, which is beneficial for both the converter and the energy storage system.
the proposed control strategies allow for a significant reduction of the active power component of the DC-link current, which in turn results in a reduction of the converter losses.
the converter topology can be utilized to achieve the desired power flow between the battery energy storage and the converter modules, as well as between the modules and the grid.
